title: Onboarding and trial — one business setup built five times across three files, one of them platform-operator-only
why:
The same business setup is coded five times. The four-stage wizard (chat → confirm → logo → CRM) exists twice in `сайт и приложение/app.html` — once in the login screen (`lgAiStage`, L6284) and once inside the chat (`onbStage`, L17526) — and twice again in `maya-os-site/index.html` (`lgAiStage` L5347 in ALogin, `onbStage` L15330 in AChat). The four conversational copies already drive one and the same backend funnel (`/onboarding/ai/drafts`, `/messages`, `/confirm`), so they are duplicated code, not duplicated product.

The fifth is different in kind. S-155 is the platform-operator path in `сайт и приложение/maya-admin.html` — roleMode `platform`, platform-owner-only per the comment at L995, and this group's only primary-navigation entry. It carries powers no tenant has: «Активировать сразу · без триала» (`POST /activate`, L1125), tenant_admin account creation (`POST /admin/tenants/{id}/users`, L1134-1136) and tenant creation itself (`POST /admin/tenants`, L1089), alongside plan selection, the 11 RU timezones, the brand and texts steps and the mock-demo-data option. Among the conversational copies the in-app one is the superset, so merging toward the landing copy would delete the CRM stage outright. This group is a reconciliation of four copies around an authority-carrying operator path, and its centre of gravity is that authority boundary rather than the removal of a redundant form.
disappear: The parallel code copies go; the entry points do not. Four implementations of the four-stage wizard become one, and the second, third and fourth are deleted as code. The operator wizard stops being a separate wizard: under one MAYA the same onboarding is a conversation with a form fallback, differing only by the authority of who is asking, so the operator's four-step form survives only as that fallback behind its authority gate — its privileged writes move, they are not retired. The trial sheet stops being its own modal and becomes an entry state of a single entitlement surface. The third STT call path stops being separately maintained and converges on the canonical voice helper, which must keep a pre-tenant ingress alongside the tenant one — one voice ingress per tenant class, not one in total. The pre-auth entry itself does not disappear: the ALogin copy becomes a pre-auth mount of the one canonical component rather than a parallel one. Nothing listed under WHAT WILL REMAIN is removed by this group; all six surfaces retire only after parity is demonstrated (RETIRE AFTER PARITY — K16).
remain:
From the conversational copies: the four declared stages (chat → confirm → logo → CRM); the CRM stage's provider chips, with unavailable providers shown as «· Скоро» in the in-app copy and DIKIDI/Salon Online/Whitelines explicitly disabled in the landing copy (L6615), the CRM user-token in a `type:'password'` field that discovery does not persist (onboarding.controller.ts L106-108), and branch discovery, search and import (L18449-18470); the confirm stage's «Данные из CRM · подтверждены» block with staff/service counts and address (L18332-18345); the «← Вернуться к диалогу» back path (L18436); the optional logo stage with its explicit skip «По желанию — можно пропустить.» (L18441-18447); weekly-schedule capture (`WK_ORDER` L16164, held only by the AChat copy in `maya-os-site/index.html`); reload-resumability (`__meReadBusinessOnboarding` L618, boot restore L38580, held only by the in-chat copy in `app.html`); and the manual, non-conversational fallback form (`lgManual` L6283, held only by the login copy — the fallback the chat-first constraint requires).

From the trial sheet: pre-session trial start with its locked state (`lgTrialLocked` L6780) and the `?trial=1` / `?start=trial` marketing deep-links (L6911), together with the paywall side's checkout (`doCheckout` L25080) and post-payment focus re-validation (L25043) — a naive merge keeps one side and loses the other. The trial length the surface is named for is 10 days.

From the operator path: plan selection, the 11 RU timezones, the brand and texts steps, the mock-demo-data option for a salon with no CRM yet, and the done screen's one-time credentials, which still need a named home. The privileged writes themselves remain and stay authority-gated: tenant creation, tenant_admin account creation and «Активировать сразу · без триала».

Voice remains an input mode and keeps its current routing — the legacy chat proxy with `authPayload({audio, transcribe_only:true})` — because onboarding is pre-tenant, and the message «Не расслышала — попробуйте ещё раз или введите текстом.» stays as the pointer to the typed fallback. Unchanged: the draft id and token stay in refs and session-scoped storage only, never in the URL or localStorage.
risk:
MEDIUM-HIGH. Four reasons, in order of weight.

First, authority. Tenant creation is the highest-consequence write in the product, and this group folds a platform-operator path into a tenant-facing conversation: `POST /activate` and tenant_admin account creation must not become reachable by a tenant. That gating is recorded as a requirement, not as a control anyone has verified — the only gate this group evidences is a front-end comment at `maya-admin.html` L995 — and the standing limitations do not close the gap: approval is role-gated, not separation-of-duties; STEP_UP_VERIFIED is unreachable; Gate 10 is measured and not enforced; the fundamental rules hold fail-closed in only 13 of 21 cases. Server-side enforcement of the operator boundary must be demonstrated at K16, not assumed.

Second, credential placement. The draft token is deliberately held in a ref and never in the URL or localStorage, and a merge that routes it through chat history leaks it. The CRM user-token must stay in a password field, and discovery must go on not persisting it. Neither may reach persisted conversation.

Third, onboarding voice fails if touched. It is pre-tenant and runs on `@Public()` opaque-token routes, so repointing it at the bearer-authenticated, `@TenantScoped()` `/ai/transcribe` breaks it entirely — no tenant token exists at that point in the funnel.

Fourth, the copies are not feature-identical and the differences are unproven: the in-app copy is the superset, the login copy alone holds the manual fallback, the in-chat copy alone holds resumability, the AChat copy alone holds the weekly schedule. Parity must be shown per copy at K16.

The level rests on that first reason. It is not HIGH: nothing here is irreversible and no surface retires before parity. It is above MEDIUM because the escalation path is unverified rather than merely delicate — and it does not rest on slug-collision or cooldown behaviour, neither of which any surface in this group attests.
user_impact: The owner signing up notices most, and the specific thing they notice is that the starting door decides the product. There are not two copies but four across three bundles: the app.html login wizard (S-008), the app.html in-app owner wizard (S-285), the ALogin copy in maya-os-site (S-075), and the AChat copy in the same file that S-285 names as a third to reconcile. The differences run in BOTH directions, so "in-app is the superset" is only true within app.html: the login copy alone has the manual, non-conversational fallback form (lgManual L6283) — the very fallback the chat-first constraint requires — and the trial sheet alone has the locked state (lgTrialLocked L6780) and the ?trial=1 / ?start=trial marketing entries, while the paywall sheet it pairs with owns checkout and post-payment re-validation (S-007); the in-app copy alone survives reload, owns CRM branch discovery/search/import and the "Данные из CRM · подтверждены" confirm block (S-285); and in maya-os-site the ALogin copy owns the CRM provider picker and logo upload while the AChat copy owns weekly-schedule capture (WK_ORDER L16164) (S-075). Logo is a stage in every copy — only the explicit skip affordance is in-app — so it is not a differentiator. Voice is likewise NOT a new benefit: all copies already accept spoken answers today through three separate STT paths (S-281, S-075); the merge changes the count of ingresses, not what the owner can do. What the owner actually gains is that the answer set, the resumability and the CRM import stop depending on where they started, and that trial activation and CRM connect become stages of one conversation. The platform operator notices second: "＋ Новый салон" is the only primary-nav row in this group and one of the 101 Maya-owned primary-nav entries that collapse to 5 (verified: 101 rows with primaryNav ∧ mayaOwned). But "becomes the same conversation asked with operator authority" is not reachable on today's substrate: the widget contract registers no onboarding or tenant-creation capability at all (0 hits), an unmapped key fails closed to STEP_UP_VERIFIED under §0.8 F50, and P-12 makes STEP_UP_VERIFIED unreachable — so until those keys are registered at a floor at or below SESSION_VERIFIED the operator path is at best a HANDOFF to a secure surface, not a chat-actuated stage. Staff and clients notice nothing here, but the scoping is pre-tenant (S-007, S-008, S-075), owner-scoped (S-281, S-285) and platform-operator-scoped (S-155, roleMode "platform") — not "pre-tenant or owner-scoped" — and the operator wizard's done screen, which hands one-time credentials for an account minted at role tenant_admin, still needs a home in the successor.
security_impact: Direction is right: no authority gate is added or strengthened here, and the honest reading is added risk that server-side work must absorb. The only genuine gain is hygiene, not a closed hole — three STT ingresses and three credential-entry implementations collapsing to one removes places where the rules below can drift apart. Running one component across the @Public() onboarding routes with opaque draft tokens (S-281) and the authenticated path means the draft id/token — today in refs plus session-scoped storage, never URL or localStorage (S-285 L17528-17529, S-075 L5348) — must not be routed through any persisted chat transcript; S-075 names exactly that draft-token leak, and names it for the draft token only. The CRM-credential claim as proposed is false for half the merge and must be split: on the pre-tenant funnel the token is a type:'password' field that is genuinely never stored (verified in code — discoverDraftCrm and importDraftCrm pass dto.apiToken straight to the CRM preview and write no token field onto the draft), but the S-155 operator wizard being folded into the same conversation PATCH/POSTs that same token to /admin/tenants/{id}/crm, where crm.service.ts stores it as encryptedApiToken. One merged credential field would therefore carry two opposite persistence contracts, which is the drift the claim assumes away. The role-gate description is also misread: the actual decorators are @Roles(PLATFORM_OWNER) on POST /admin/tenants and on POST /admin/tenants/{id}/activate (both @TenantScoped), and @Roles(PLATFORM_OWNER, TENANT_ADMIN) + @TenantScoped + @RequiresQuota(STAFF) on POST /admin/tenants/{id}/users — where "role tenant_admin" is the DEFAULT ROLE OF THE ACCOUNT BEING CREATED (CreateTenantUserDto restricts it to TENANT_OWNER/TENANT_ADMIN/BRANCH_MANAGER/STAFF), not the caller gate. So "minting an admin user" is not new exposure: a tenant_admin can already do that inside its own tenant today, quota-bounded; the genuinely operator-only powers are tenant creation and "Активировать сразу · без триала". The "role-gated only, not separation-of-duties" tag must be dropped: that frozen limitation is about the approval path, where canDecide resolves approvalPolicy 'owner' to any owner-role member including the initiator, and S-155 says nothing about it. These endpoints exclude tenant roles from /activate outright, which is a role-boundary gate, not a four-eyes gate; what the merge removes is bundle-level defence in depth — operator-only branches stop living in a separate admin bundle a tenant never loads — leaving that server-side gate as the sole barrier. Two further server-side obligations belong here: converging the onboarding voice ingress must not redirect it onto the bearer-authenticated @TenantScoped() /ai/transcribe, because onboarding is pre-tenant and holds no tenant token, which would break onboarding voice entirely (S-281); and any operator-authority tenant create/activate offered in chat needs its capability key registered, since an unregistered key fails closed to the unreachable STEP_UP_VERIFIED (§0.8 F50, P-12) and a key registered at risk tier 'restricted' is permanently withheld.
